    user = User.query.get(uid)
    user.name = request.json["name"]
    db.session.commit()
evidence.why: The user ID comes from the URL and is used directly to load a user record without checking that the record belongs to the authenticated user.

findings.recommendation: Bind the update to the authenticated user.

verification.notes: The endpoint loads a user by the id from the URL and updates the name without checking that the user id matches the authenticated user.

findings.title: BOLA in PATCH /users/<int:uid>: missing owner verification

evidence.why: The user ID is taken from the URL and the record is updated without verifying ownership.

findings.recommendation: Ensure the target user belongs to the authenticated session.

verification.notes: The PATCH handler updates the user record directly from the request JSON without any visible ownership check or cast. No role or global filter is shown in the provided context.

findings.title: Profile update allows role change

evidence.why: $user->role = $_POST['role']; no restriction on role field

findings.recommendation: Do not bind role field from request; set role server‑side only

verification.notes: The code assigns $_POST['role'] directly to $user->role without any restriction, allowing privilege escalation.

findings.title: SQL Injection in classic-asp/shop/order.asp:12

evidence.code: Set rs2 = conn.Execute("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = " & sid & " AND user_id = " & CLng(Session("UserID")))
evidence.why: sid from Request.QueryString("sid") concatenated without sanitization

findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries

verification.notes: Both the order id and user id are cast to integers before concatenation, preventing SQL injection.
